source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Change all/random setting to non-default in this BIOS function.
3. Save and reboot.
4. Boot in to BIOS and  check your setting still exist.
5. Press load default,save and reboot.
6. Boot in to BIOS,setting in this function should match the SPEC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error log happen.
2. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
3. Check your setting still exist.
4. The default setting should matches SPEC."

original_test_intent: Verify that selected BIOS boot controls and target ordering persist after save/reboot and return to documented defaults after Load Default without booting an unintended disk, installer, network target or shell or stranding the installed OS.
original_method: Manually change an approved set of Boot-page values, save/reboot and verify both Setup persistence and the actual boot target; then Load Default, save/reboot, compare fields with SPEC and confirm the intended system remains recoverable.
manual_activity: A human must identify the Boot-page controls, navigate Setup, select only approved targets, complete the save/default operations and visually verify firmware state and actual target selection. Read-only boot inventory is auxiliary.
required_inputs: Board/BIOS identity and UEFI/CSM/Secure Boot state
Stable mapping of firmware boot entries to exact disk, partition, network or removable target
Approved non-default ordering/options and SPEC defaults
Expected OS and boot mode for each phase
Console, BMC/OOB, compatible recovery media and backups
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or select an unverified installer, shell, network service or writable removable device.
Identify disks by persistent hardware/filesystem identity, not mutable enumeration alone.
Do not alter an active encrypted/RAID boot path without validated unlock and recovery.
Stop on wrong target, installer/write prompt, missing entry, boot loop, OS failure or management loss.
Restore the approved final boot policy.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only firmware boot entries, disk/filesystem identity, boot mode, OS identity, logs and BMC health.
Correlate the observed boot with the approved target matrix and flag ambiguity.
Do not drive BIOS, select boot media, authorize writes or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve exact fields, entry/device mapping, target behavior, defaults and recovery.
Perform/capture firmware persistence, actual-boot and default-restoration phases.
Evaluate target identity and system health and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly refuses agent BIOS execution. No source command exists; an OS boot-entry listing cannot prove which firmware choice was made before OS startup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the BIOS workflow and add approved read-only entry/device/OS identity evidence. Do not substitute an OS bootloader change or software reboot policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The two save/reboot phases, null script and 5/20-minute fields are preserved; all/random remains source text only.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a firmware-entry-to-device/artifact map using persistent identities, approve each ordering/control change, and capture both the displayed firmware state and the target that actually executed through persistence, defaults and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact firmware revision, storage/network/removable topology and installed OS/bootloader.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, bootloader, OS/kernel and inventory-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform Boot-page definitions and approved OS/bootloader/recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds persistent target identity and protects against accidental installer, network or wrong-disk boot.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; retains field lifecycle and adds proof of actual boot target.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Entry mapping, boot expectations, defaults and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Boot-entry numbers and disk enumeration may change; evidence must use stable identifiers.

project_override_considerations: A project may select only specific boot controls or targets. Completion must state the approved entry/device matrix and cannot imply coverage of excluded PXE, removable, shell or alternate-OS paths.
expected_evidence: Platform identity, entry-to-device map, approved matrix and recovery
Baseline Boot page, entries, disks, boot mode and OS identity
Non-default captures, persistence and actual intended target
Load Default captures, SPEC comparison and actual default target
Final boot policy, system/BMC health, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for persistence and default restoration. The target and value matrix is missing project information rather than a contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The boot-settings intent is clear. Exact target identity and recovery must be supplied before execution but are ordinary readiness gates.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on manual operation and adds target-identity and write-protection boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Preserves its boot and recovery evidence improvements while correcting classification to MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates human Setup acceptance from agent evidence and makes actual boot-target identity part of coverage.

review_improvement: Prevents a visually correct boot order from being accepted without proving the intended artifact actually booted and without exposing the host to unintended writable media.
independent_technical_reasoning: Core configuration, target selection and pre-OS visual verification require an engineer. Automated OS evidence starts after the decisive boot choice and therefore cannot make the case partial or fully automated.
no_automatic_retry: Do not automatically repeat boot-order changes or reboots after the wrong target, a write-capable environment or boot failure appears; preserve evidence and obtain engineer direction.
